description: The one floor in this design with a single out, and the fixture that keeps the modules carrier from being named where it cannot help. `createInterface` is published by its block, so its floor names the key to write. `close` is not: it lives on a type alias, and an alias is a name for a type rather than a symbol with a member table the walk can descend into — so it has no key under any specifier, and the message says the bridge is all there is rather than sending the reader to write an entry that would reach nothing.

diagnostics.message: Call to `createInterface` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay, override or baseline entry colors it, so it is assumed to throw. Your outs, in precedence order: bridge this call with `try`/`catch`; assert the color in `nothrow.overrides.json` under `modules` → "readline" → `createInterface`; or install or write an `@no-throw/*` overlay carrying that same key. It is declared in an ambient `declare module` block, which no package entry point publishes, so no manifest can key it.

Call to `lines.close` escapes this `@nothrow` function: it is declared without a body — an ambient declaration, a `.d.ts`, or a value known only by its function type — and no mark, manifest, overlay, override or baseline entry colors it, so it is assumed to throw. Your out: bridge this call with `try`/`catch` — it is declared in the ambient module "readline", which publishes it under no name, so no carrier has a key that reaches it.
